aoristic.e: English aorist Proto-Indo-European *-ikos Proto-Italic *-ikos Latin -icuslbor. Old French -iquebor. Middle English -ik English -ic English aoristic From aorist + -ic.

aortal.e: English aorta Proto-Indo-European *h₂el-der.? Proto-Italic *-ālis Latin -ālisbor. Old French -albor. ▲ Latin -ālis Old French -elbor. ▲ Latin -ālisbor. Middle English -al English -al English aortal From aorta + -al.

d.g: Of or pertaining to the aorta or the aortic valve.

aortic.e: From aorta + -ic. By surface analysis, aort- + -ic.

d.g: A verb paradigm found in certain languages, usually an unmarked form or one that expresses the perfective or aorist aspect.

d.g: The great artery which carries the blood from the heart to all parts of the body except the lungs; the main trunk of the arterial system.

aorta.e: Borrowed from Ancient Greek ἀορτή (aortḗ, “the arteries springing from the heart”), from ἀορτέω (aortéō), lengthened form of ἀείρω (aeírō, “to lift, raise”).
